doc.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014

title: Jazz as the true American art form; is it better now
summary: Jazz is America's one true art form, honored everywhere but at home; musicians no longer need drugs.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: this 40 years that we are here, is jazz. Jazz could not have happened anywhere in the world. Everything is secondhand European or it comes from Asia. The American people should be so proud that jazz came from here. Because it’s honored everywhere in the world but not here. I don’t understand. I don’t know why.
Has it gotten any better? I mean we have Jazz at Lincoln Center and now almost every college, especially bigger colleges, you can go and study it.

And musicians don’t have to go on drugs anymore because it’s better. It’s a better situation. But I don’t understand why it cannot be really like in Europe. Why rock & roll is so big here. I don’t understand.
